body:
## Summary

How Linewright works a pull request it opened moves out of the single `if` chain in `reconcile::in_review` and into a new `working_pull` module. The new module is shaped like the Working a pull request table and the model's `Pr` record. Behavior does not change.

```diff
 decisions
   for each pull request Linewright opened
-    in_review(ticket, pr, memory, policy, now)   # each fact worked out where it is used
+    pull_work(ticket, pr, memory, policy, now)   # only maps a Row to an Action or a Wait
+      working_pull::facts(pr, memory, policy, now) -> Facts
+      working_pull::row(&Facts) -> Row           # the first row that holds, one branch per row
```

```text
src/
├── reconcile.rs      # pull_work: Row -> Action / Wait; in_review, restarted_at, tried_rebase, merge, is_held gone
└── working_pull.rs   # Facts, Checks, GitHub, Row, row, facts
```

The facts and rows still read the earlier prose, not the table:

- feedback is what came after Linewright's last push
- the unmergeable update runs once per head (`Row::Rebase`)
- the blocked-merge comment is keyed by its requirements
- a draft is merged or held in the same step that marks it ready
- `Row::HandBackNotRebaseable` is a row the table does not have

Comments in `working_pull` say the next ticket changes these to the table's.

## Evidence

- **Before:** no seam picks a row from the facts alone. A row could only be reached through `reconcile::decisions` with a whole snapshot.
  **After:** `working_pull::the_row_is_the_first_that_holds` gives `row` one `Facts` per row. Each `Facts` also makes as many later rows hold as it can. The test checks that `row` returns the expected row.
- Every existing reconcile and integration test passes, and no expected value changed.
- The review found one behavior change, which is now fixed:
  - Under `--auto-merge` by rebase, a clean draft whose rebaseability GitHub had not reported would have been marked ready.
  - It now waits, as it did before, through `GitHub::RebaseNotReported`.
  - A new reconcile test pins this: `with_auto_merge_by_rebase_a_green_draft_whose_rebaseability_is_unknown_waits_as_a_draft` expects no action and `Wait::MergeState`.
- `scripts/check` passes: `ok: fmt markdown compose css clippy test doc`.
  - In this session's environment, cargo did not set `CARGO_BIN_EXE_fake-claude`. That breaks the test build on `main` too.
  - To get a run, the checks used a local, uncommitted patch to that path in `tests/integration/common/harness.rs`.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

It only changes structure. Reverting it restores the old chain.

**Blast Radius:** pull-requests

A wrong mapping would change what Linewright does with its own open pull requests: rework, update, fix-ci, hand back, mark ready, comment or merge. The existing reconcile tests cover each of those, and they pass unchanged.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Closes #931
title: Work a pull request by a facts record and the first row that holds

body:
## Summary

A merged spec change is now worked through its own issue, like any other, instead of being designed on its pull request (`docs/specs/sources_of_work.md`, Spec changes).

```diff
 reconcile, for each merged pull request
-  claim it, start a design run on it (Subject::SpecChange)
+  a spec change Linewright may take up         -> OpenSpecChangeIssue { let_go: false }
+  assigned by hand, not yet taken up          -> OpenSpecChangeIssue { let_go: true }
+  assigned by hand, taken up already          -> UnassignFromPull { comment }

 factory: OpenSpecChangeIssue (an action with no run)
+  create "Spec change: <PR title>", body "Opened for the spec change in #N.",
+    labeled ready-for-agent and the required label where the repository has it
+  then unassign Linewright from the spec change, if let_go
```

- **Taken up.** A spec change counts as taken up once an issue Linewright opened links it, open or closed, or once it carries `linewright:designed` (or `linewright:spec-processed`). The snapshot gains `spec_change_issues`. The GitHub store fills it from its existing managed-issues index, which holds every open issue and those closed since the windows' `read_since`. That is a superset of "created since the lookback window opened", so no extra query is needed.
- **Removed.** `Subject::SpecChange`, `Work::DesignSpecChange`, `Memory::ended_cuts`, the spec-change discard, `CutItem`, the `design-spec-change` result, its schema (`docs/specs/results/design-spec-change.schema.json`, which is outside the spec glob and no longer referenced) and the `cut-spec-change` prompt part. Also removed: the spec change's own card, its waits, `Ended::NothingToBuild` and the `WaitingForDesign` / `SpecChangeBeingDesigned` details.
- **`Tracks` is now `is_tracking`.** A spec change's issue is a tracking issue the same way any issue is.
- **`merged_row`.** A new function in `lifecycle` holds the merged pull request's rows of the Working an item and Steering tables, and returns its own `MergedRow` enum.
- **Views.** `explain` shows a merged spec change as Merged and left alone, with its issue as a child ("its issue"). The item page's Spec change fact names the spec change of a spec change's issue.
- **User guide.** `docs/user-guide.md` ("Changing the spec" and the label list) now describes the new flow. It is user-facing documentation, so it needs your approval.

## Evidence

- **Before:** a merged spec change started `Work::DesignSpecChange` on the pull request, and the board showed it as a card in Ready or Working.
  **After:** these tests pass:
  - `pipeline::a_merged_spec_change_opens_one_issue_which_is_claimed_and_designed`: one issue labeled `ready-for-agent`; the next poll claims it and cuts it; after a restart and another poll there is still one issue, and the pull request has no labels, assignees or comments.
  - `pipeline::a_spec_change_whose_issue_closed_before_the_done_window_is_not_taken_up_again`: Done window 1 day, lookback 30 days, issue closed 3 days ago, so no second issue.
  - `pipeline::linewright_assigned_to_a_spec_change_not_yet_taken_up_opens_its_issue_then_unassigns_itself`.
  - `reconcile::*`: designed or spec-processed, merged before the lookback window, unmarked, Linewright's own and other-branch spec changes are not taken up; taking up is not held back by the ceiling, the usage limit or a drain.
  - `lifecycle::a_merged_pull_request_is_worked_by_the_first_row_that_holds`: every merged row, with the exact let-go comments.
  - `store::github::tests::the_index_holds_a_closed_spec_changes_issue_while_it_reads_back_to_its_closing`, on a newly recorded payload of closed issue #485.
  - Contract test `a_snapshot_holds_a_spec_changes_issue_closed`.
- `scripts/check`: 1557 tests run, 1557 passed.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Nothing is migrated or deleted on GitHub. Old-format tracking issues ("Tickets for the spec change in #N") still count as taking up their spec change, so nothing already designed is taken up again.

**Blast Radius:** spec-changes

New merged spec changes get an issue instead of a pull-request design. A spec change Linewright worked under an earlier release still shows as a Merged card in Done until it leaves the Done window, as the Managed items "Worked" rule says. If the required label is set but the repository lacks it, the spec change's issue is opened without it and so is not marked; assigning Linewright to the issue by hand works it, the same as for any other unmarked issue.

Closes #907
title: Take up a spec change by opening its issue

body:
The row "ready for review | GitHub blocks the merge, and Linewright has not commented on it this round | comments naming what GitHub requires" (`pull_requests.md`, Working a pull request) leaves open which comments count as "commented".

Linewright comments on a pull request for other reasons within a round: when it marks a draft ready for review ("CI is green: ready for review.") and when a fix-ci or update run ends. Read literally, those count, and the requirements comment would almost never be posted, because a draft is marked ready in the same round in which its merge is blocked. `pull_request.qnt` sets `commented` only from this row's own comment.

The design for #930 takes the model's reading. Only the comment naming what GitHub requires counts. Linewright keeps a record of when it posted one, rather than reading its own comments (Comments, "For people").

**The spec change needed:** say which comments count, for example "... and Linewright has not commented on it this round naming what GitHub requires".

Found while working on #930.
title: Which comments count as "Linewright has commented on it this round" for a blocked merge

body:
## What to build

#914 in the code: Linewright leaves a merged pull request it did not open as it is, except to take up a spec change not yet taken up (the Working an item and Steering tables in `docs/specs/repository.md`). Assigned to a merged pull request that is not a spec change, or to a spec change already taken up, it no longer unassigns itself with a comment.

`lifecycle::merged_row` keeps only taking up a spec change: on its own when Linewright may, and when assigned to one not yet taken up, after which it unassigns itself. Its let-go row goes, and so does the arm in `reconcile` that applies it.

The two other #914 rows hold already and need only a test each. Status labels are cleaned up only on an open issue. `linewright:stalled` is cleared only from an open item.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Linewright assigned to a merged pull request whose files are not in the spec, or to a merged spec change already taken up, gets no unassignment and no comment.
- [ ] Linewright assigned to a merged spec change not yet taken up opens its issue, then unassigns itself, as before.
- [ ] Functional-core tests show that a closed issue with two status labels keeps both, and that a merged or closed pull request carrying `linewright:stalled` keeps it.
- [ ] `scripts/check` passes.
title: Leave a merged pull request alone except to take up a spec change

body:
## What to build

Linewright works a pull request it opened as the Working a pull request table in `docs/specs/pull_requests.md` gives, first row that holds, as the design on the tracking issue sets out. Three rows change from what the code does today:

- **Feedback.** A comment or review from anyone other than Linewright stays feedback until a rework run that was given it ends done. A fix-ci or update push no longer answers it. A rework run that answers without pushing does not start again. A comment posted after a rework run pushed but before it ended is addressed by the next rework run.
- **The unmergeable update.** An update run for a branch no allowed method can merge starts only while no run has ended on the pull request since its last push. This replaces remembering a tried rebase per head in memory, so a restart does not repeat it, and neither does a fix-ci run that already brought the branch up to date.
- **The blocked-merge comment.** It is posted once a round, while Linewright has not commented on it this round, no longer when the requirements change. The record of the comment's time replaces the requirements-keyed record. Without a record, a ready pull request that GitHub blocks counts as commented.

A round starts when Linewright opens the pull request, when a rework run on it ends (however it ends) and when Linewright is assigned to it again. Both counts start again with each round: the fix-ci runs that have ended (`ci-attempts`) and the failed merges (two). Memory keeps every ended run on a pull request, with how and when it ended.

The order follows the table. A draft is marked ready for review in its own step, before any merge, blocked-merge comment or wait for what GitHub requires. A branch GitHub reports not rebaseable after its update is merged as any other and, if the merge fails twice, handed back with GitHub's reason. It no longer gets the separate "not rebaseable" hand-back.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of the table's 14 rows has a functional-core test in which it is the first row that holds, with expected values taken from the table.
- [ ] Feedback: a rework run that ends done without a push starts no new rework. A comment between a rework run's push and its end starts one. A fix-ci push leaves feedback standing.
- [ ] Update: a pull request GitHub reports not rebaseable gets one update run after each push, also across a restart. It gets none once a fix-ci run has ended since that push.
- [ ] Round: fix-ci attempts and failed merges count from the round's start, and a rework run ending, done or not, starts a new round.
- [ ] The blocked-merge comment is posted once a round, and a change in requirements within a round posts no new comment.
- [ ] With `--auto-merge`, a draft with green checks is marked ready first, and is merged on a later poll.
- [ ] `RememberRebase`, `MarkReadyForMergeState` and `Merge`'s draft flag are gone.
- [ ] `scripts/check` passes.
title: Work a pull request as the Working a pull request table gives

body:
## What to build

The structure change for #930, with no change in behavior. How Linewright works a pull request it opened moves out of the single `if` chain in `reconcile::in_review` into a new `working_pull` module, shaped like the Working a pull request table in `docs/specs/pull_requests.md` and the record in `docs/specs/model/pull_request.qnt`:

- a `Facts` record, worked out once from the pull request, memory and the policy;
- a `Row` enum;
- `row(&Facts) -> Row`, the first row that holds, one branch per row.

`reconcile` then maps the row to its action or wait. The design on the tracking issue gives the modules and their interfaces.

The rows and facts keep today's readings: feedback after Linewright's last push, the unmergeable update once per head, the blocked-merge comment by requirements, and a draft merged or held in the same step that marks it ready. The next ticket changes them to the table's. Where today's order differs from the table, keep today's order here, and say in a comment that the next ticket changes it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `working_pull` holds `Facts`, `Row` and `row`, and `in_review` is gone. `reconcile` only maps a row to an `Action` or a `Wait`.
- [ ] The facts are worked out in one function, not inside the row branches.
- [ ] Every existing reconcile and integration test passes without changing any expected value.
- [ ] New tests through the functional core give `row` a `Facts` for each row and check that the row is the first to hold.
- [ ] `scripts/check` passes.
title: Work a pull request by a facts record and the first row that holds
